 By BVM Sportsdesk, 9h ago The Bulls are still at the beginning of their rebuild, executive vice president Bryson Graham says, with progress hinging on player development, accountability and building a sustainable identity under coach Tiago Splitter. As Chicago prepares to face Boston, the team may have an unexpected offensive strength: getting to the free-throw line.
 By the Numbers Chicago is 1-2.
 The Bulls made 56 of 60 free throws across games against Milwaukee and Washington — 93.3%.
 The Celtics game is scheduled for Oct. 26, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. Central.
 Yes, But Free throws have been a bright spot, but Chicago’s three-point shooting has struggled. Turning paint pressure into better perimeter looks could help address that weakness, while the team’s early-stage rebuild leaves questions about how quickly its young core can deliver meaningful progress.
 What's Next Against Boston, the Bulls’ keys are to make Jayson Tatum and Paul George work without giving up open shots, secure defensive rebounds, push the pace, create threes through drives and ball movement, and avoid a third-quarter collapse.
 Bottom Line Chicago’s free-throw accuracy offers a potential foundation, not proof of a finished offensive identity. The rebuild’s real test is whether the Bulls can turn that strength—and development from their young players—into consistent progress.
